newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures slow ascent on origin sales.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures slow ascent on origin sales.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures continued their rally but by Thursday the ascent had been slowed by renewed origin offers at the highs, traders said.
Activity was again centred on May/July switches, trading up to $20 at one stage. Volume totalled a modest 2,686 lots.
Benchmark May gained $20 to end the midsession at $1,630 a tonne after a high of $1,635. July stood $16 up at $1,646.
London's advance still fell short compared with New York, where prices soared to a two-and-a-half year peak on Wednesday as fresh arabica supply worries gripped the market.
May/May arbitrage gapped at a wide $1.34 cents a lb.
European traders said the New York arabica futures remained vulnerable to further spike higher.
"There are two strikes coming up, the certified stocks are low and the May spread is widening," said one. "A few roasters are not covered and I think May could continue to rise."
Traders' nerves were rattled by news of possible disruptions to supplies in Columbia and Brazil.
A strike by Colombian truck drivers was set to begin at midnight Saturday and looked certain to deepen near-term supply concerns.
Brazil's two key coffee ports after Santos were expected to be hit by a 48-hour national strike by stevedores due to begin at 1000 GMT Friday, unions said.
Union officials in Rio de Janeiro and Vitoria said they were going to take part in the national strike, the second in two weeks following a 24-hour stoppage on April 4.
Well-supplied robustas are being weighed by arrivals from the main Indonesian harvest.
Analysts said the technical picture in London could improve if May clears above $1,668, the April 2 high. But it could struggle to regain a foothold at the recent peak of just above $1,800.
